facts.raw_span: painful swelling of the calves
no evidence of deep venous thrombosis or soft-tissue infection
elevated LDH and CK
negative autoimmune serology
CT scan showed no lymphoma relapse but diffuse subcutaneous edema
elevated CRP, transaminases, CK, troponin I, myoglobin, and LDH
reduced plasma protein, albumin, and IgG
MRI of the thighs showed diffuse intramuscular and extramuscular edema
muscle biopsy demonstrated interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates
acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis
Cardiac MRI confirmed myocarditis
CSF analysis showed leukocyte count 329/μl, lactate 3.5 mmol/L, and protein 79.6 mg/dl

concepts.why: Elevated CK and muscle biopsy demonstrating interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates support the diagnosis of polymyositis.
Cardiac MRI confirmation and elevated troponin I support the diagnosis of myocarditis.
Acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis and MRI showing diffuse intramuscular and extramuscular edema support the diagnosis of rhabdomyolysis.
CSF analysis and spinal MRI demonstrating a hyperintense lesion support the diagnosis of transverse myelitis.
Acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis and reduced plasma protein support the diagnosis of acute kidney injury.

Elevated CK and muscle biopsy demonstrating interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates, although not specific to dermatomyositis, could also support this diagnosis in the context of skin involvement.

Elevated CK and muscle biopsy demonstrating interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates, although not specific to inclusion body myositis, could also support this diagnosis in the context of slowly progressive muscle weakness.
Cardiac MRI confirmation and elevated troponin I, in the context of systemic inflammation, could support the diagnosis of cardiac sarcoidosis.

rationales.F01: Painful swelling of the calves is a common symptom of polymyositis.
rationales.F03: Elevated LDH and CK are indicative of muscle damage, which is consistent with polymyositis and rhabdomyolysis.
rationales.F06: Elevated CRP, transaminases, CK, troponin I, myoglobin, and LDH suggest a systemic inflammatory response and muscle damage.
rationales.F09: Muscle biopsy demonstrating interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates is characteristic of polymyositis.
rationales.F11: Cardiac MRI confirmation of myocarditis suggests cardiac involvement, which is consistent with myocarditis and cardiac sarcoidosis.
rationales.F12: CSF analysis showing elevated leukocyte count, lactate, and protein is indicative of central nervous system inflammation, which is consistent with transverse myelitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: Polymyositis best explains the combination of muscle pain, elevated LDH and CK, and muscle biopsy findings, despite negative autoimmune serology, which is not uncommon in this condition.
